stem:
Rakesh's class asks why the Northern Hemisphere has summer in June while the Southern Hemisphere has winter then.

Which reason is correct?

options.text: Earth's tilted axis stays pointed the same way as Earth revolves, so in June the Northern Hemisphere gets more direct sunlight and longer days.
In June the Northern Hemisphere is closer to the Sun because of the tilt.
In June the Northern Hemisphere has winter.
In June both hemispheres have summer.

teacher.key_rationale: Seasons come from Earth's maintained tilt as it revolves, which changes sunlight intensity and day length by hemisphere. June summer in the north is not because that hemisphere is closer, nor is it winter there, nor summer in both hemispheres.
